<section class="ds-section" id="figures"><h2>What the data show</h2>
<p>The preferred total-trade real index falls from 100 in 1929 to <strong>85.11 in 1933</strong>. It rises to <strong>95.84 in 1934</strong>, a 12.61% increase over 1933, and reaches <strong>102.78 in 1937</strong>. In 1935, nominal depreciation of <strong>1.39%</strong> accompanies a <strong>2.60% fall</strong> in the real index: relative-price movements offset the nominal change. These calculations use the preferred current-year-weighted chains in <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-annual.csv">Annual EER</a>.</p>
<p>Formula choice matters near the 1929 benchmark. All four total-trade chained real indices exceed 100 in 1937. In 1938, their positions relative to 100 differ. The direct current-weighted index supplies a separate comparison with a different construction.</p>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><caption>Total-trade REER by specification, 1929 = 100</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Specification</th><th class="num" scope="col">1933</th><th class="num" scope="col">1937</th><th class="num" scope="col">1938</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Current-year chain — preferred</th><td class="num">85.11</td><td class="num">102.78</td><td class="num">100.33</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Lagged-year chain</th><td class="num">83.72</td><td class="num">100.96</td><td class="num">98.14</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Törnqvist chain</th><td class="num">84.41</td><td class="num">101.87</td><td class="num">99.23</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Fixed-1929-weight chain</th><td class="num">85.31</td><td class="num">105.92</td><td class="num">102.76</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Direct current-weighted index</th><td class="num">86.26</td><td class="num">98.87</td><td class="num">96.39</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="ds-small">Source: <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-all-series.csv">All series</a>, total-trade real indices. The explorer’s shaded range describes the four chain specifications; it is not a confidence interval. Changes in annual indices are descriptive and do not identify the within-year timing or causal effect of a monetary-policy decision.</p>

<section class="ds-section" id="methods"><h2>How the series are constructed</h2>
<p>The preferred series are <strong>current-year-weighted geometric chains</strong>. Let <em>e</em> be crowns per unit of harmonised foreign currency and <em>q = e × P<sub>foreign</sub> / P<sub>CS</sub></em> the corresponding bilateral real rate. The annual change of the effective index is the trade-weighted average of bilateral log changes:</p>
<div class="ds-equation"><code>ln I(t) − ln I(t−1) = Σᵢ w(i,t) [ln z(i,t) − ln z(i,t−1)]</code></div>
<p>Here <em>z = e</em> for NEER and <em>z = q</em> for REER. Chained levels are rebased to 1929 = 100. The workbook calls this the Paasche-type chain. Separate indices use total-trade, export and import weights; the six preferred series appear in <em>Annual EER</em>, and all variants in <em>All series</em>.</p>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><caption>Available index specifications</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Formula</th><th scope="col">Weighting of bilateral movements</th><th scope="col">Trade bases</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Current-year chain (Paasche-type)</th><td>Current-year partner shares in each annual log change.</td><td>Total, exports, imports</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Lagged-year chain (Laspeyres-type)</th><td>Previous-year partner shares in each annual log change.</td><td>Total, exports, imports</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Törnqvist chain</th><td>Average of current- and previous-year partner shares.</td><td>Total, exports, imports</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Fixed-1929-weight chain</th><td>The 1929 partner shares in every annual link.</td><td>Total, exports, imports</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Direct current-weighted index</th><td>Current shares applied to bilateral levels relative to the 1929 reference.</td><td>Total only</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p>Weights sum to one <em>within the basket</em>. Coverage measures the basket’s share of national trade. Total-trade coverage is 85.45% in 1929 and 73.37% in 1937. The coverage chart displays the reported export, import and total-trade shares on a 70–100% vertical scale. The partner heatmap displays normalised basket weights.</p>
<p>CPI-based REER measures broad relative consumer prices. CPI changes can reflect indirect taxes and subsidies and are only indirectly related to exporters’ production costs; the index does not measure non-price competitiveness. See the <a href="https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/balance_of_payments_and_external/hci/html/index.en.html">ECB’s discussion of CPI-based competitiveness indicators</a>.</p>
<h3 id="analysis-methods">Annual changes and the nominal–real decomposition</h3>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Measure</th><th scope="col">Calculation</th><th scope="col">Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Annual percentage change</th><td><code>100 × [I(t) / I(t−1) − 1]</code></td><td>Change relative to the preceding calendar year.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Annual log change</th><td><code>100 × ln[I(t) / I(t−1)]</code></td><td>Log points, used for the exact additive decomposition.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Relative-price component</th><td><code>C(t) = 100 × REER(t) / NEER(t)</code></td><td>Cumulative chained relative-price movements for matched chains, with 1929 = 100.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Real-change decomposition</th><td><code>100 Δln REER = 100 Δln NEER + 100 Δln C</code></td><td>Nominal and relative-price components add to the real log change.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Optional three-year average</th><td><code>[I(t−1) + I(t) + I(t+1)] / 3</code></td><td>Centered descriptive average in levels, requiring all three annual observations within the same sample segment.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Alternative reference year</th><td><code>I(t; b) = 100 × I(t) / I(b)</code></td><td>Changes displayed levels; annual growth rates are invariant.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p>For matched chains, the relative-price term is the corresponding weighted foreign CPI log change minus the domestic CPI log change. Its level is a cumulative chain. The direct-current ratio also reflects the changing allocation of weights; the explorer reserves the inflation decomposition for chain specifications.</p>
<p>The three-year average uses complete calendar windows, including observations outside a cropped display range when available. It does not cross the boundary between the early extension and the analytical core. Endpoints and windows containing missing observations remain blank. The original annual points stay visible. Rebasing applies the same scaling factor to observations and their average.</p>
<p class="ds-small">Annual changes use the preceding observed calendar year: the 1925 change uses 1924 even when the chart begins in 1925. Unavailable REER values in 1920–1922 remain missing. The analytical extension contains no interpolated monthly observations.</p>
</section>
<section class="ds-section" id="provenance"><h2>Sources and the early extension</h2>
<p>The reader edition distinguishes the <strong>1920–1924 early extension</strong> from the <strong>1925–1938 analytical core</strong>. The explorer defaults to the analytical core. The full-period levels view uses a logarithmic scale so that the exceptionally large early observations and later annual movements can both be inspected.</p>
<p>The construction supplement supplies the released <strong>266-row bilateral input panel</strong>, five currency-conversion rules and a reproducible index calculation. All <strong>455 available index observations</strong> agree with the publication archive. Independent reconstruction from the bilateral inputs agrees to floating-point precision. The <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/early-year-links.csv">early-year diagnostics</a> identify the contributions of the recorded quotations and price inputs to the preferred chain.</p>
<p>These checks verify the released calculations. They do not independently verify every historical transcription or the comparable unit basis of every early price observation. The source manuscript describes annual averages; the exact within-year averaging convention is not encoded in its calculation files. The source notes distinguish verified numerical transformations from these limits of the underlying documentation.</p>
<details><summary>Currency-unit rules in the released calculation</summary><p>The input quotation is crowns per reported foreign-currency unit. The calculation multiplies it by the recorded factor before constructing nominal and real rates. The final year below is an implementation cutoff for annual observations, rather than a legal currency-reform date.</p>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Partner</th><th class="num" scope="col">Multiplier</th><th scope="col">Years to which it is applied</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Germany</th><td class="num">1,000,000,000,000</td><td>1920–1924</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Austria</th><td class="num">10,000</td><td>1920–1924</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Poland</th><td class="num">1,800,000</td><td>1920–1923</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Hungary</th><td class="num">12,500</td><td>1920–1926</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Belgium–Luxembourg</th><td class="num">5</td><td>1920–1926</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p class="ds-small">Source: the publication archive’s <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/currency-unit-rules.csv">currency-unit ledger</a>. Other partner-years use a factor of one. The source ledger identifies the conversion references and their verification scope.</p></details>
<p><a download href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/construction-package.zip">Construction inputs and reproduction code (ZIP)</a> · <a download href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/bilateral-inputs.csv">Bilateral inputs (CSV)</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/bilateral-data-dictionary.csv">Input dictionary</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/cpi-source-ledger.csv">CPI source labels</a> · <a href="https://github.com/adamdittrich/adamdittrich.github.io/blob/main/assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/reproduce_indices.py">Reconstruct the indices</a> · <a href="assets/files/datasets/eer-documentation/validation-report.json">Numerical verification</a></p>
<details><summary>Partner basket and missing observations</summary><p>Austria; Belgium–Luxembourg; France; Germany; Hungary; Italy; Netherlands; Poland; Romania; Sweden; Switzerland; United Kingdom; United States; Yugoslavia.</p><p>NEER is available for 1920–1938 and CPI-based REER for 1923–1938. Missing real observations remain blank in the CSV files and are represented by gaps in charts. The sample designation is included in the analytical download.</p></details>
<p>The source ledger and provenance notes identify the source materials behind the reader edition. The extension’s metadata records source checksums, variable definitions, formulas, sample conventions and licence scope. The build script reproduces the analytical tables and static figures from the supplied EER tables.</p>

<section class="ds-section" id="ljungberg"><h2>Relation to Jonas Ljungberg’s database</h2>
<p><a href="https://www.lusem.lu.se/node/309">Ljungberg’s <em>Nominal and Real Effective Exchange Rates for Europe, 1870–2016</em></a> provides the broader European comparison. His <a href="https://portal.research.lu.se/en/publications/nominal-and-real-effective-exchange-rates-for-europe-1870-2016-so/">2019 methodological paper</a> explains the use of annual current-year trade weights, CPI adjustment and the depreciation-upward convention. This workbook implements geometric chains and supplies alternative formulas explicitly; it should not be treated as an identical copy of Ljungberg’s series.</p>
<div class="ds-table-scroll"><table class="ds-table ds-comparison"><caption>The Czechoslovak comparison</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Feature</th><th scope="col">Ljungberg’s interwar benchmark</th><th scope="col">This reader workbook</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Included partners</th><td>8 in Appendix A of the Cliometrica article</td><td>14</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Share of national trade in 1929</th><td>69%</td><td>85.45%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Partner selection</th><td>Austria, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Soviet Union, United Kingdom and United States</td><td>The fourteen partners listed above; the Soviet Union is not in this basket</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Index formula</th><td>The 2024 article’s Figure 1 uses Paasche fixed-base indices (note 20)</td><td>Preferred current-year-weighted geometric chains; alternative chains and a direct current-weighted variant are supplied</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Where to find the comparison</th><td>European database and <em>Competitive devaluations in the 1930s: myth or reality?</em>, Appendix A</td><td><em>Annual EER</em>, <em>All series</em>, <em>Partner weights</em> and <em>Basket coverage</em></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p>The samples differ rather than forming a simple nested expansion. A comparison should match the reference year, direction, weighting formula and price coverage before interpreting differences between the indices.</p>
<p class="ds-reference">Ljungberg, Jonas. 2019. <em>Nominal and Real Effective Exchange Rates for Europe, 1870–2016: Some Methodological Issues.</em> Lund Papers in Economic History, 2019:200. <a href="https://portal.research.lu.se/en/publications/nominal-and-real-effective-exchange-rates-for-europe-1870-2016-so/">Publication record</a> · <a href="https://lup.lub.lu.se/search/files/66677473/LUPEH_200.pdf">Paper PDF</a> · <a href="https://www.lusem.lu.se/node/309">Database and download</a>.</p>
<p class="ds-reference">Ljungberg, Jonas. 2024. “Competitive devaluations in the 1930s: myth or reality?” <em>Cliometrica</em> 18, 151–189. Published online 18 December 2022. <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/s11698-022-00262-9">doi:10.1007/s11698-022-00262-9</a>. Appendix A identifies the eight Czechoslovak partners and 69% coverage in 1929.</p>
